newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China and Britain agree on Chinese force for HK.
newsitem.headline: China and Britain agree on Chinese force for HK.

text.p: China and Britain have agreed an advance party of Chinese troops will arrive in Hong Kong next week in preparation for the territory's July 1 return to Chinese sovereignty, a Hong Kong government spokesman said on Tuesday.
The party of 40 People's Liberation Army soldiers would prepare facilities and communications for the future PLA garrison, the spokesman said in a statement.

Tuesday's announcement was a major breakthrough. The issue of a PLA advance guard, its size and role, and whether it would be armed, has stalled Sino-British diplomatic talks on details of the handover for many months.
"The two sides of the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group have reached agreement on the arrival of 40 advance personnel of the future Garrison in Hong Kong from April 21," the spokesman said.
"They will not be armed and will not enjoy any special legal status or JLG privileges and immunities," the spokesman said.

"The duties of advance personnel are to make practical preparations for the PLA to take over the responsibility for the defence of Hong Kong, including familiarisation with the military sites, liaison with the British Forces and the Hong Kong Government, and coordination of communications support."
